{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1791837234889,"sessionID":"ses_ece2f83deffefealO0yC5b638e","part":{"partID":"prt_131d0a7da0010xnPZAJbC2q0WK","sessionID":"ses_ece2f83deffefealO0yC5b638e","messageID":"msg_131d0a2e4001O2yjiZakUxoM7M","type":"tool","id":"toolu_vrtx_018Gt1CR5b7SuzRLdXStbDg3","tool":"write","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"path":"/private/var/folders/qm/d729jn6n47z5nxpkpf361l9w0000gn/T/agent-eval/v2/cases/case-007-rough-api/artifacts/result.md","content":"# Requirements Elicitation Package\n\n## Understanding\n\n**Requested outcome:** Users can submit invoice documents through a browser interface. The system accepts each submission, processes it asynchronously, and persists the processed result. Invoices that are malformed, invalid, or otherwise unprocessable are handled without silent failure.\n\n**Proposed system boundary:** The system under specification is a web-based invoice upload and processing service. It exposes a browser interface for submissions, an asynchronous processing pipeline, and a persistence layer for results.\n\n**Source material classification:**\n\n| Statement | Kind |\n|---|---|\n| \"Users can upload invoices\" | Goal / behavioral obligation |\n| \"Use a React form\" | Design idea (framework choice — kept out of normative sentences) |\n| \"put the work on a Redis queue\" | Design idea (queue technology — kept out of normative sentences) |\n| \"store the result in a PostgreSQL table\" | Design idea (storage technology — kept out of normative sentences) |\n| \"handle bad invoices gracefully\" | Goal / behavioral obligation (vague — needs clarification on \"bad\" and \"gracefully\") |\n\nThe technology choices (React, Redis, PostgreSQL) are implementation constraints the requester has imposed. They are preserved here as design context and in the Assumptions section, but they are intentionally excluded from normative sentences because requirements describe observable behavior at system boundaries, not implementation structures.\n\n---\n\n## Clarifying Questions\n\nThe following questions represent the highest-value gaps. Each, if left unanswered, would allow two reasonable implementers or verifiers to produce visibly different behavior.\n\n**Q1 — Accepted file formats and size limits (affects C1, C2)**\nWhat file types may a user upload (e.g., PDF, PNG, CSV, XML)? Is there a maximum file size? What happens when an unsupported type or oversized file is submitted?\n\n**Q2 — Definition of \"bad invoice\" (affects C4, C5)**\n\"Bad invoices\" is ambiguous. Does it include: malformed files (corrupt, unreadable), files of a wrong type, files with missing required fields (e.g., no invoice number, no total), invoices that fail a business rule (e.g., amount exceeds a threshold), or all of the above? The answer determines how many distinct failure candidates are needed.\n\n**Q3 — Definition of \"gracefully\" (affects C4, C5)**\nWhat observable behavior is expected when a bad invoice is detected?\n- Is the user notified in the browser at the time of submission, asynchronously after processing, or both?\n- Is a failed invoice persisted (e.g., with an error status), discarded, or returned to the user?\n- Is the user allowed to correct and resubmit?\n\n**Q4 — User identity and authentication (affects C1, C4)**\nMust the submitting user be authenticated? Is invoice ownership tracked per user, or are all submissions treated as anonymous? This affects the observable submission response (e.g., whether a user-specific identifier is returned or stored).\n\n**Q5 — Submission response and acknowledgement (affects C1)**\nWhen a user submits a valid invoice, what does the system return immediately? Options include: a submission identifier the user can reference, a status indicator, or no immediate acknowledgement. The answer determines whether a synchronous acknowledgement requirement is needed.\n\n**Q6 — Result observability and retrieval (affects C3)**\nAfter a submitted invoice is processed, how does a user or downstream consumer access the stored result? Is there a retrieval endpoint? Can the user check status? If no retrieval behavior is specified, the stored result is unobservable at the named boundary.\n\n**Q7 — Duplicate submissions (affects C1)**\nWhat happens when a user uploads the same invoice file more than once? Is each submission treated independently, or is deduplication required?\n\n**Q8 — Processing timeout (affects C4)**\nIf asynchronous processing does not complete within some time window, is that treated as a failure? What is the time boundary, and is the user notified?\n\n---\n\n## Candidate Requirements\n\n### Candidate 1\n\n- **Status:** needs clarification\n- **Template:** Event-driven\n- **Requirement:** When a user submits an invoice file, the Invoice Upload Service shall accept the submission and return an acknowledgement to the user.\n- **Source intent and rationale:** The primary stated goal is that users can upload invoices. A submission event at the browser interface triggers the system. The immediate response (acknowledgement) is implied but not specified — Q1 (file types, size) and Q5 (what acknowledgement looks like) are open.\n- **Implementability contract**\n  - System boundary: Browser interface exposed by the Invoice Upload Service\n  - Responsible system: Invoice Upload Service\n  - Actor: Authenticated or anonymous user (open — see Q4)\n  - Affected interfaces: Browser form submission endpoint (HTTP request/response)\n  - Inputs and data definitions: Invoice file — format(s) and size limits are unresolved (Q1)\n  - Preconditions, state, feature scope, and trigger: User submits an invoice file via the browser interface\n  - Observable normal, alternate, and failure response: System accepts the submission; returns an acknowledgement — content and form of acknowledgement are unresolved (Q5); behavior for unsupported file types is unresolved (Q1)\n  - Quantities, units, limits, timing, ordering, and tolerances: File size limit unresolved (Q1); response timing unresolved (Q5)\n  - Domain terms, dependencies, and unresolved decisions: \"submit\" = user action to send a file; \"acknowledgement\" = undefined observable response (Q5); accepted file formats undefined (Q1); authentication requirement undefined (Q4)\n- **Verification contract**\n  - Setup, state, input data, and stimulus: A user opens the invoice submission interface and submits a file of an accepted type within any size limit\n  - Observable evidence or oracle: HTTP response received by the browser after submission\n  - Expected result: The system returns an acknowledgement (content undefined — Q5)\n  - Pass/fail criteria, including scope, thresholds, units, and timing: Pass when an acknowledgement is received; fail when no response or an error is returned — thresholds unresolved\n  - Boundary, negative, and failure cases: Unsupported file type (Q1), oversized file (Q1), unauthenticated user (Q4), duplicate submission (Q7) — all unresolved\n  - Required data, instrumentation, assessment, or external evidence: Access to the submission endpoint; a valid invoice file in an accepted format\n  - Observable at the named boundary alone: yes\n  - If no, internal evidence needed and rationale: N/A\n\n---\n\n### Candidate 2\n\n- **Status:** needs clarification\n- **Template:** Event-driven\n- **Requirement:** When a user submits an invoice file, the Invoice Upload Service shall validate the submission before accepting it.\n- **Source intent and rationale:** \"Handle bad invoices gracefully\" implies that the system distinguishes valid from invalid invoices. Validation at the submission boundary is a necessary companion to C1. The specific validation rules are unresolved (Q1, Q2).\n- **Implementability contract**\n  - System boundary: Browser interface / submission endpoint\n  - Responsible system: Invoice Upload Service\n  - Actor: User\n  - Affected interfaces: Browser form submission endpoint\n  - Inputs and data definitions: Invoice file; validation rules are unresolved — file type, size, required fields, business rules (Q1, Q2)\n  - Preconditions, state, feature scope, and trigger: User submits a file\n  - Observable normal, alternate, and failure response: If validation passes, submission is accepted; if validation fails, submission is rejected — rejection response content is unresolved (Q2, Q3)\n  - Quantities, units, limits, timing, ordering, and tolerances: Validation rule thresholds unresolved (Q1, Q2)\n  - Domain terms, dependencies, and unresolved decisions: \"validate\" — rules are unresolved; \"bad invoice\" is undefined (Q2)\n- **Verification contract**\n  - Setup, state, input data, and stimulus: Submit a file known to be invalid (e.g., wrong type, missing field) and a file known to be valid\n  - Observable evidence or oracle: System response distinguishes accepted from rejected submissions\n  - Expected result: Valid file accepted; invalid file rejected with an observable signal\n  - Pass/fail criteria, including scope, thresholds, units, and timing: Unresolved — validation rules not yet defined\n  - Boundary, negative, and failure cases: Each category of \"bad invoice\" (Q2); boundary file sizes (Q1)\n  - Required data, instrumentation, assessment, or external evidence: Test files for each validation case; knowledge of defined validation rules\n  - Observable at the named boundary alone: yes\n  - If no, internal evidence needed and rationale: N/A\n\n---\n\n### Candidate 3\n\n- **Status:** needs clarification\n- **Template:** Event-driven\n- **Requirement:** When an accepted invoice is ready for processing, the Invoice Processing Service shall process the invoice and persist the result.\n- **Source intent and rationale:** The source requests asynchronous processing (\"put the work on a queue\") and storage of the result (\"store the result\"). This requirement describes the observable outcome of that pipeline: a processed result is persisted. The content of \"the result\" and how it is observable are not specified (Q6).\n- **Implementability contract**\n  - System boundary: Processing pipeline output / persistence boundary\n  - Responsible system: Invoice Processing Service\n  - Actor: System (triggered by a queued work item, not directly by a user action at this stage)\n  - Affected interfaces: Persistence store (write interface); optional retrieval interface (Q6)\n  - Inputs and data definitions: Accepted invoice (format as resolved in C1/C2); processed result — fields and schema are unresolved (Q6)\n  - Preconditions, state, feature scope, and trigger: An accepted invoice is placed in the processing queue\n  - Observable normal, alternate, and failure response: Result is persisted — observable schema and retrieval method are unresolved (Q6); failure path during processing is addressed in C4/C5\n  - Quantities, units, limits, timing, ordering, and tolerances: Processing time limit unresolved (Q8); result retention period unresolved\n  - Domain terms, dependencies, and unresolved decisions: \"result\" — content and structure undefined (Q6); retrieval behavior undefined (Q6)\n- **Verification contract**\n  - Setup, state, input data, and stimulus: An accepted invoice is submitted and queued for processing\n  - Observable evidence or oracle: After processing completes, the result is retrievable (Q6 — retrieval method undefined)\n  - Expected result: A result record exists and is accessible\n  - Pass/fail criteria, including scope, thresholds, units, and timing: Unresolved — result content, schema, and retrieval path undefined (Q6)\n  - Boundary, negative, and failure cases: Processing failure (C4); timeout (Q8); duplicate processing (Q7)\n  - Required data, instrumentation, assessment, or external evidence: Access to the persistence store or retrieval endpoint; a known accepted invoice as input\n  - Observable at the named boundary alone: no\n  - If no, internal evidence needed and rationale: The persistence of the result is only verifiable by reading the persistence store or a retrieval endpoint, neither of which is yet defined (Q6). Without a defined retrieval path, the verification contract cannot be completed.\n\n---\n\n### Candidate 4\n\n- **Status:** needs clarification\n- **Template:** Unwanted behavior\n- **Requirement:** If a submitted invoice fails validation, then the Invoice Upload Service shall reject the submission and notify the user of the reason for rejection.\n- **Source intent and rationale:** \"Handle bad invoices gracefully\" implies the user is informed when their invoice is not accepted. This candidate covers the synchronous validation-failure path. \"Gracefully\" and \"reason for rejection\" are not yet measurable (Q2, Q3).\n- **Implementability contract**\n  - System boundary: Browser interface / submission endpoint\n  - Responsible system: Invoice Upload Service\n  - Actor: User\n  - Affected interfaces: Browser form submission response\n  - Inputs and data definitions: Invalid invoice file; rejection reason — defined by validation rule set (Q1, Q2)\n  - Preconditions, state, feature scope, and trigger: User submits a file that fails validation\n  - Observable normal, alternate, and failure response: Submission is rejected; user receives a notification with the rejection reason — form and content of notification are unresolved (Q3)\n  - Quantities, units, limits, timing, ordering, and tolerances: Notification timing (synchronous vs. deferred) unresolved (Q3)\n  - Domain terms, dependencies, and unresolved decisions: \"gracefully\" — no agreed measure (Q3); \"reason for rejection\" — message format and specificity undefined\n- **Verification contract**\n  - Setup, state, input data, and stimulus: Submit an invoice file that fails a known validation rule\n  - Observable evidence or oracle: The submission endpoint response contains a rejection indicator and a reason\n  - Expected result: Submission rejected; reason message visible to user\n  - Pass/fail criteria, including scope, thresholds, units, and timing: Unresolved — \"gracefully\" and reason content are not measurable without Q2/Q3 answers\n  - Boundary, negative, and failure cases: Each category of invalid invoice (Q2); user-visible response content\n  - Observable at the named boundary alone: yes\n  - If no, internal evidence needed and rationale: N/A\n\n---\n\n### Candidate 5\n\n- **Status:** needs clarification\n- **Template:** Unwanted behavior\n- **Requirement:** If processing of an accepted invoice fails, then the Invoice Processing Service shall record the failure and notify the submitting user.\n- **Source intent and rationale:** \"Handle bad invoices gracefully\" also covers failures detected during asynchronous processing (after submission was accepted). This is a distinct path from synchronous validation failure (C4). Whether the user is notified asynchronously and how failure is recorded are unresolved (Q3, Q6).\n- **Implementability contract**\n  - System boundary: Processing pipeline / persistence and notification boundary\n  - Responsible system: Invoice Processing Service\n  - Actor: System (failure condition); submitting user (notification recipient)\n  - Affected interfaces: Persistence store (failure record write); user notification channel (undefined — Q3)\n  - Inputs and data definitions: Accepted invoice that fails during processing; failure record — fields undefined (Q6)\n  - Preconditions, state, feature scope, and trigger: An accepted and queued invoice encounters a processing failure\n  - Observable normal, alternate, and failure response: Failure is recorded; user is notified — notification channel, timing, and content are unresolved (Q3); whether the invoice is retried or discarded is unresolved\n  - Quantities, units, limits, timing, ordering, and tolerances: Retry count and interval unresolved; notification timing unresolved (Q3)\n  - Domain terms, dependencies, and unresolved decisions: \"processing failure\" — categories undefined (Q2); notification channel undefined (Q3); \"record the failure\" — schema and retrieval undefined (Q6)\n- **Verification contract**\n  - Setup, state, input data, and stimulus: Submit an accepted invoice that is engineered or known to fail during processing\n  - Observable evidence or oracle: Failure record exists in the persistence store; user receives notification\n  - Expected result: Failure is recorded and user is informed\n  - Pass/fail criteria, including scope, thresholds, units, and timing: Unresolved — notification channel and failure record schema undefined (Q3, Q6)\n  - Boundary, negative, and failure cases: Repeated processing failures; failure after partial processing; timeout expiry (Q8)\n  - Required data, instrumentation, assessment, or external evidence: Access to the persistence store; evidence of user notification delivery; engineered failure scenario\n  - Observable at the named boundary alone: no\n  - If no, internal evidence needed and rationale: The failure record is only verifiable via the persistence store or a retrieval endpoint (both undefined — Q6). User notification requires evidence of delivery through the notification channel (undefined — Q3).\n\n---\n\n## Suggested Supporting Requirements\n\n**SR-1 — File size and type constraint**\n*Relationship:* Boundary companion to C1 and C2\n*Missing behavior:* The system has no stated constraint on the file types or sizes it accepts. Without a defined boundary, the submission endpoint behavior for unsupported or oversized inputs is undefined.\n*Suggestion:* Consider adding a requirement that the system rejects files that do not conform to the accepted type list or exceed a stated maximum size, and that it notifies the user of the specific constraint violated.\n*Precondition:* Q1 must be answered first.\n\n**SR-2 — Submission acknowledgement with tracking identifier**\n*Relationship:* Required companion to C1\n*Missing behavior:* Once a valid invoice is accepted, the user has no stated mechanism to know whether processing succeeded or failed later.\n*Suggestion:* Consider requiring the system to return a unique submission identifier at acceptance time, enabling the user or a downstream system to correlate later status or failure notifications.\n*Precondition:* Q5 and Q6 must be answered to determine whether a retrieval path exists.\n\n**SR-3 — Processing status retrieval**\n*Relationship:* Interface companion to C3 and C5\n*Missing behavior:* The result is persisted (C3) but no retrieval behavior is specified. The verification contract for C3 and C5 cannot be completed without a defined retrieval path.\n*Suggestion:* Consider specifying that the system exposes an interface by which an authorized caller can retrieve the processing status and result for a given submission.\n*Precondition:* Q6 must be answered.\n\n**SR-4 — Duplicate submission handling**\n*Relationship:* Boundary companion to C1\n*Missing behavior:* If a user uploads the same invoice twice, the expected behavior is undefined.\n*Suggestion:* Determine whether the system should detect duplicates (and on what key — file hash, invoice number, etc.), reject them, or process each independently. Add a requirement once the policy is decided.\n*Precondition:* Q7 must be answered.\n\n**SR-5 — Processing timeout and retry**\n*Relationship:* Failure-path companion to C3 and C5\n*Missing behavior:* If processing does not complete within a time boundary, the outcome is undefined. The user may wait indefinitely.\n*Suggestion:* Consider specifying a maximum processing duration after which the system treats the invoice as a processing failure and applies the C5 behavior (record failure, notify user).\n*Precondition:* Q8 must be answered.\n\n**SR-6 — User authentication and authorization**\n*Relationship:* Required companion to C1 (if ownership is required)\n*Missing behavior:* Whether users must authenticate before submitting is unstated. If invoice ownership matters (e.g., a user should only see their own processing results), authentication is a prerequisite.\n*Suggestion:* Determine whether the service requires authentication and, if so, specify the authentication boundary and the behavior when an unauthenticated user attempts to submit.\n*Precondition:* Q4 must be answered.\n\n---\n\n## Consistency Findings\n\n**Finding 1 — Gap: C3 result is unobservable without a retrieval path**\nC3 requires that a result be persisted, but no candidate or suggestion yet defines how that result is retrieved. Without a retrieval interface, the persistence obligation in C3 cannot be independently verified, and C5's failure record is similarly unobservable. SR-3 addresses this gap. Resolution: specify a retrieval interface requirement (accept SR-3, or define the observable retrieval behavior in C3).\n\n**Finding 2 — Gap: Synchronous vs. asynchronous failure notification are not yet separated**\nC4 covers synchronous validation failure (at submission time). C5 covers asynchronous processing failure (after acceptance). These are intentionally split. However, if Q3 reveals that the user is notified of both failure types through the same channel, the notification behavior should be checked for consistency between C4 and C5 to avoid contradictory messages for the same invoice.\n\n**Finding 3 — Precedence question: Validation in C2 vs. processing failure in C5**\nC2 implies validation occurs before the invoice enters the queue. C5 implies some bad invoices pass validation and fail during processing. The boundary between these two failure modes is not yet defined (Q2). If validation is complete at the boundary (C2), the processing failure in C5 should be limited to processing-specific failures (e.g., a service dependency failure, parsing error not caught at submission). Resolution: Q2 must define which failure types are caught at which stage.\n\n**Finding 4 — Overlap risk: \"Bad invoice\" spans C2, C4, and C5**\nThe undefined scope of \"bad invoice\" risks overlap between C2 (validation), C4 (synchronous rejection), and C5 (asynchronous processing failure). Once Q2 is answered, re-check that each candidate covers a distinct failure category with no unintended overlap.\n\n**Finding 5 — Gap: No candidate covers the normal user journey end-to-end**\nNo candidate currently specifies what the user observes after a successful end-to-end flow (submission → processing → result available). SR-2 and SR-3 address parts of this gap, but a complete happy-path observable sequence is not yet captured. Resolution: once Q5 and Q6 are answered, add a candidate or refine C1 and C3 to cover the full observable lifecycle.\n\n---\n\n## Assumptions\n\n**A1 — Technology choices are design constraints, not requirements.**\nThe source names React, Redis, and PostgreSQL. These are treated as implementation design choices imposed by the requester, not as system behaviors. They are excluded from normative sentences. If any of these technologies impose externally visible constraints (e.g., Redis queue item size limits, PostgreSQL row-size limits), those constraints should be expressed as observable behavioral requirements when their values are known.\n\n**A2 — Asynchronous processing is implied by \"queue.\"**\nThe source's mention of a queue implies that invoice processing does not occur synchronously with the user's submission. This assumption separates the submission response (C1) from the processing and persistence behavior (C3).\n\n**A3 — \"Gracefully\" means the user is informed, not that failures are silently discarded.**\nIn the absence of a definition, \"handle bad invoices gracefully\" is interpreted to mean the user receives an observable, actionable signal when their invoice is rejected or fails processing. This interpretation is provisional and subject to Q3.\n\n**A4 — \"Result\" refers to a structured output of invoice processing, not the original invoice file.**\nC3 uses \"result\" to mean whatever the processing pipeline produces (e.g., extracted data, a parsed record, a status). The schema and content of this result are undefined and must be resolved via Q6.\n\n**A5 — The system boundary is a single service.**\nThe source implies a single system. If there are separate services (upload service, processing service, notification service), each requires its own boundary and responsible-system declaration. The candidates name notional services for clarity but do not prescribe a deployment architecture.\n\n---\n\n## Rationale and Context\n\nThe source request combines a user-facing goal (\"users can upload invoices\") with implementation directives (React, Redis, PostgreSQL) and a quality aspiration (\"handle bad invoices gracefully\"). The goal is to make this request implementable and verifiable by separating what the system must do (observable behavior) from how it is built (technology choices).\n\nThe split between C4 (synchronous rejection) and C5 (asynchronous processing failure) reflects a structural reality: once the source says \"put the work on a queue,\" there are now two distinct failure moments with potentially different notification paths. Both must be specified, and Q2–Q3 are the minimum required to make them verifiable.\n\nThe five candidates cover the primary behavioral obligations implied by the request. All are marked `needs clarification` because one or more material questions remain open in each implementability or verification contract. No candidate has been promoted to `candidate` or `ready for review` while those questions are unresolved.\n\n---\n\n## Review Status\n\n| Candidate | Status | Blocking questions |\n|---|---|---|\n| C1 — Invoice submission and acceptance | needs clarification | Q1, Q4, Q5, Q7 |\n| C2 — Submission validation | needs clarification | Q1, Q2 |\n| C3 — Processing and result persistence | needs clarification | Q6, Q8 |\n| C4 — Synchronous rejection and user notification | needs clarification | Q2, Q3 |\n| C5 — Asynchronous processing failure and user notification | needs clarification | Q2, Q3, Q6, Q8 |\n\n**All five candidates are `needs clarification`.** The minimum set of questions to advance any candidate to `candidate` status is **Q2** (definition of \"bad invoice\") and **Q3** (definition of \"gracefully\"), which unblock C2, C4, and C5. Q1 (file types and size) unblocks C1 and C2. Q5 and Q6 are needed before C1 and C3 can pass their verification contracts.\n\nNo requirements have been approved. This package is the output of one elicitation pass. The system accepts each submission, processes it asynchronously, and persists the processed result. Invoices that are malformed, invalid, or otherwise unprocessable are handled without silent failure.\\n\\n**Proposed system boundary:** The system under specification is a web-based invoice upload and processing service. It exposes a browser interface for submissions, an asynchronous processing pipeline, and a persistence layer for results.\\n\\n**Source material classification:**\\n\\n| Statement | Kind |\\n|---|---|\\n| \\\"Users can upload invoices\\\" | Goal / behavioral obligation |\\n| \\\"Use a React form\\\" | Design idea (framework choice — kept out of normative sentences) |\\n| \\\"put the work on a Redis queue\\\" | Design idea (queue technology — kept out of normative sentences) |\\n| \\\"store the result in a PostgreSQL table\\\" | Design idea (storage technology — kept out of normative sentences) |\\n| \\\"handle bad invoices gracefully\\\" | Goal / behavioral obligation (vague — needs clarification on \\\"bad\\\" and \\\"gracefully\\\") |\\n\\nThe technology choices (React, Redis, PostgreSQL) are implementation constraints the requester has imposed. They are preserved here as design context and in the Assumptions section, but they are intentionally excluded from normative sentences because requirements describe observable behavior at system boundaries, not implementation structures.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Clarifying Questions\\n\\nThe following questions represent the highest-value gaps. Each, if left unanswered, would allow two reasonable implementers or verifiers to produce visibly different behavior.\\n\\n**Q1 — Accepted file formats and size limits (affects C1, C2)**\\nWhat file types may a user upload (e.g., PDF, PNG, CSV, XML)? Is there a maximum file size? What happens when an unsupported type or oversized file is submitted?\\n\\n**Q2 — Definition of \\\"bad invoice\\\" (affects C4, C5)**\\n\\\"Bad invoices\\\" is ambiguous. Does it include: malformed files (corrupt, unreadable), files of a wrong type, files with missing required fields (e.g., no invoice number, no total), invoices that fail a business rule (e.g., amount exceeds a threshold), or all of the above? The answer determines how many distinct failure candidates are needed.\\n\\n**Q3 — Definition of \\\"gracefully\\\" (affects C4, C5)**\\nWhat observable behavior is expected when a bad invoice is detected?\\n- Is the user notified in the browser at the time of submission, asynchronously after processing, or both?\\n- Is a failed invoice persisted (e.g., with an error status), discarded, or returned to the user?\\n- Is the user allowed to correct and resubmit?\\n\\n**Q4 — User identity and authentication (affects C1, C4)**\\nMust the submitting user be authenticated? Is invoice ownership tracked per user, or are all submissions treated as anonymous? This affects the observable submission response (e.g., whether a user-specific identifier is returned or stored).\\n\\n**Q5 — Submission response and acknowledgement (affects C1)**\\nWhen a user submits a valid invoice, what does the system return immediately? However, if Q3 reveals that the user is notified of both failure types through the same channel, the notification behavior should be checked for consistency between C4 and C5 to avoid contradictory messages for the same invoice.\\n\\n**Finding 3 — Precedence question: Validation in C2 vs. processing failure in C5**\\nC2 implies validation occurs before the invoice enters the queue. C5 implies some bad invoices pass validation and fail during processing. The boundary between these two failure modes is not yet defined (Q2). If validation is complete at the boundary (C2), the processing failure in C5 should be limited to processing-specific failures (e.g., a service dependency failure, parsing error not caught at submission). Resolution: Q2 must define which failure types are caught at which stage.\\n\\n**Finding 4 — Overlap risk: \\\"Bad invoice\\\" spans C2, C4, and C5**\\nThe undefined scope of \\\"bad invoice\\\" risks overlap between C2 (validation), C4 (synchronous rejection), and C5 (asynchronous processing failure). Once Q2 is answered, re-check that each candidate covers a distinct failure category with no unintended overlap.\\n\\n**Finding 5 — Gap: No candidate covers the normal user journey end-to-end**\\nNo candidate currently specifies what the user observes after a successful end-to-end flow (submission → processing → result available). SR-2 and SR-3 address parts of this gap, but a complete happy-path observable sequence is not yet captured. Resolution: once Q5 and Q6 are answered, add a candidate or refine C1 and C3 to cover the full observable lifecycle.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Assumptions\\n\\n**A1 — Technology choices are design constraints, not requirements.**\\nThe source names React, Redis, and PostgreSQL. These are treated as implementation design choices imposed by the requester, not as system behaviors. They are excluded from normative sentences. If any of these technologies impose externally visible constraints (e.g., Redis queue item size limits, PostgreSQL row-size limits), those constraints should be expressed as observable behavioral requirements when their values are known.\\n\\n**A2 — Asynchronous processing is implied by \\\"queue.\\\"**\\nThe source's mention of a queue implies that invoice processing does not occur synchronously with the user's submission. This assumption separates the submission response (C1) from the processing and persistence behavior (C3).\\n\\n**A3 — \\\"Gracefully\\\" means the user is informed, not that failures are silently discarded.**\\nIn the absence of a definition, \\\"handle bad invoices gracefully\\\" is interpreted to mean the user receives an observable, actionable signal when their invoice is rejected or fails processing. This interpretation is provisional and subject to Q3.\\n\\n**A4 — \\\"Result\\\" refers to a structured output of invoice processing, not the original invoice file.**\\nC3 uses \\\"result\\\" to mean whatever the processing pipeline produces (e.g., extracted data, a parsed record, a status). The schema and content of this result are undefined and must be resolved via Q6.\\n\\n**A5 — The system boundary is a single service.**\\nThe source implies a single system. If there are separate services (upload service, processing service, notification service), each requires its own boundary and responsible-system declaration. The candidates name notional services for clarity but do not prescribe a deployment architecture.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Rationale and Context\\n\\nThe source request combines a user-facing goal (\\\"users can upload invoices\\\") with implementation directives (React, Redis, PostgreSQL) and a quality aspiration (\\\"handle bad invoices gracefully\\\"). The goal is to make this request implementable and verifiable by separating what the system must do (observable behavior) from how it is built (technology choices).\\n\\nThe split between C4 (synchronous rejection) and C5 (asynchronous processing failure) reflects a structural reality: once the source says \\\"put the work on a queue,\\\" there are now two distinct failure moments with potentially different notification paths. Both must be specified, and Q2–Q3 are the minimum required to make them verifiable.\\n\\nThe five candidates cover the primary behavioral obligations implied by the request. All are marked `needs clarification` because one or more material questions remain open in each implementability or verification contract. No candidate has been promoted to `candidate` or `ready for review` while those questions are unresolved.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Review Status\\n\\n| Candidate | Status | Blocking questions |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| C1 — Invoice submission and acceptance | needs clarification | Q1, Q4, Q5, Q7 |\\n| C2 — Submission validation | needs clarification | Q1, Q2 |\\n| C3 — Processing and result persistence | needs clarification | Q6, Q8 |\\n| C4 — Synchronous rejection and user notification | needs clarification | Q2, Q3 |\\n| C5 — Asynchronous processing failure and user notification | needs clarification | Q2, Q3, Q6, Q8 |\\n\\n**All five candidates are `needs clarification`.** The minimum set of questions to advance any candidate to `candidate` status is **Q2** (definition of \\\"bad invoice\\\") and **Q3** (definition of \\\"gracefully\\\"), which unblock C2, C4, and C5. Q1 (file types and size) unblocks C1 and C2. Q5 and Q6 are needed before C1 and C3 can pass their verification contracts.\\n\\nNo requirements have been approved. This package is the output of one elicitation pass. The candidates are provisional until the clarifying questions are answered and both quality contracts are re-evaluated.\\n\"}"},"time":{"start":1791837120474,"end":1791837234889}}}}

{"type":"text","timestamp":1791837331073,"sessionID":"ses_ece2f83deffefealO0yC5b638e","part":{"id":"prt_131d26d86001LyAez80UzMxoD9","sessionID":"ses_ece2f83deffefealO0yC5b638e","messageID":"msg_131d26756001eXnjkWE9pqH3Er","type":"text","text":"The file has been written to `artifacts/result.md`. Here is the complete portable Requirements Elicitation Package:\n\n---\n\n# Requirements Elicitation Package\n\n## Understanding\n\n**Requested outcome:** Users can submit invoice documents through a browser interface. The system accepts each submission, processes it asynchronously, and persists the processed result. Invoices that are malformed, invalid, or otherwise unprocessable are handled without silent failure.\n\n**Proposed system boundary:** The system under specification is a web-based invoice upload and processing service. It exposes a browser interface for submissions, an asynchronous processing pipeline, and a persistence layer for results.\n\n**Source material classification:**\n\n| Statement | Kind |\n|---|---|\n| \"Users can upload invoices\" | Goal / behavioral obligation |\n| \"Use a React form\" | Design idea — framework choice, kept out of normative sentences |\n| \"put the work on a Redis queue\" | Design idea — queue technology, kept out of normative sentences |\n| \"store the result in a PostgreSQL table\" | Design idea — storage technology, kept out of normative sentences |\n| \"handle bad invoices gracefully\" | Goal / behavioral obligation — vague; needs clarification on \"bad\" and \"gracefully\" |\n\nThe technology choices (React, Redis, PostgreSQL) are implementation constraints the requester has imposed. They are preserved in context and the Assumptions section but are intentionally excluded from normative sentences, which describe observable behavior at system boundaries, not internal structures.\n\n---\n\n## Clarifying Questions\n\n**Q1 — Accepted file formats and size limits** *(affects C1, C2)*\nWhat file types may a user upload (e.g., PDF, PNG, CSV, XML)? Is there a maximum file size? What happens when an unsupported type or oversized file is submitted?\n\n**Q2 — Definition of \"bad invoice\"** *(affects C4, C5)*\n\"Bad invoices\" is ambiguous. Does it include: malformed files (corrupt, unreadable), files of the wrong type, files with missing required fields (e.g., no invoice number, no total), invoices that fail a business rule (e.g., amount exceeds a threshold), or all of the above?\n\n**Q3 — Definition of \"gracefully\"** *(affects C4, C5)*\nWhat observable behavior is expected when a bad invoice is detected?\n- Is the user notified in the browser at submission time, asynchronously after processing, or both?\n- Is a failed invoice persisted (e.g., with an error status), discarded, or returned to the user?\n- Is the user allowed to correct and resubmit?\n\n**Q4 — User identity and authentication** *(affects C1, C4)*\nMust the submitting user be authenticated? Is invoice ownership tracked per user, or are all submissions treated as anonymous?\n\n**Q5 — Submission response and acknowledgement** *(affects C1)*\nWhen a user submits a valid invoice, what does the system return immediately? A submission identifier the user can reference, a status indicator, or no immediate acknowledgement?\n\n**Q6 — Result observability and retrieval** *(affects C3, C5)*\nAfter a submitted invoice is processed, how does a user or downstream consumer access the stored result? Is there a retrieval endpoint? Can the user check status? Without a defined retrieval path, the stored result is unobservable at the named boundary.\n\n**Q7 — Duplicate submissions** *(affects C1)*\nWhat happens when a user uploads the same invoice file more than once? Is each submission treated independently, or is deduplication required?\n\n**Q8 — Processing timeout** *(affects C4, C5)*\nIf asynchronous processing does not complete within some time window, is that treated as a failure? What is the time boundary, and is the user notified?\n\n---\n\n## Candidate Requirements\n\n### Candidate 1 — Invoice submission and acceptance\n\n- **Status:** needs clarification\n- **Template:** Event-driven\n- **Requirement:** When a user submits an invoice file, the Invoice Upload Service shall accept the submission and return an acknowledgement to the user.\n- **Source intent and rationale:** The primary stated goal is that users can upload invoices. A submission event at the browser interface triggers the system. The immediate response is implied but not specified — Q1 (file types, size) and Q5 (what acknowledgement looks like) are open.\n- **Implementability contract**\n  - System boundary: Browser interface exposed by the Invoice Upload Service\n  - Responsible system: Invoice Upload Service\n  - Actor: User — authentication requirement open (Q4)\n  - Affected interfaces: Browser form submission endpoint (HTTP request/response)\n  - Inputs and data definitions: Invoice file — format(s) and size limits unresolved (Q1)\n  - Preconditions, state, feature scope, and trigger: User submits an invoice file via the browser interface\n  - Observable normal, alternate, and failure response: System accepts the submission; returns an acknowledgement — content and form of acknowledgement unresolved (Q5); behavior for unsupported file types unresolved (Q1)\n  - Quantities, units, limits, timing, ordering, and tolerances: File size limit unresolved (Q1); response timing unresolved (Q5)\n  - Domain terms, dependencies, and unresolved decisions: \"acknowledgement\" is undefined (Q5); accepted file formats undefined (Q1); authentication requirement undefined (Q4)\n- **Verification contract**\n  - Setup, state, input data, and stimulus: A user opens the invoice submission interface and submits a file of an accepted type within any size limit\n  - Observable evidence or oracle: HTTP response received by the browser after submission\n  - Expected result: The system returns an acknowledgement — content undefined (Q5)\n  - Pass/fail criteria: Pass when an acknowledgement is received; fail when no response or an error is returned — thresholds unresolved\n  - Boundary, negative, and failure cases: Unsupported file type (Q1), oversized file (Q1), unauthenticated user (Q4), duplicate submission (Q7) — all unresolved\n  - Required data, instrumentation, assessment, or external evidence: Access to the submission endpoint; a valid invoice file in an accepted format\n  - Observable at the named boundary alone: yes\n\n---\n\n### Candidate 2 — Submission validation\n\n- **Status:** needs clarification\n- **Template:** Event-driven\n- **Requirement:** When a user submits an invoice file, the Invoice Upload Service shall validate the submission before accepting it.\n- **Source intent and rationale:** \"Handle bad invoices gracefully\" implies the system distinguishes valid from invalid invoices. Validation at the submission boundary is a necessary companion to C1. The specific validation rules are unresolved (Q1, Q2).\n- **Implementability contract**\n  - System boundary: Browser interface / submission endpoint\n  - Responsible system: Invoice Upload Service\n  - Actor: User\n  - Affected interfaces: Browser form submission endpoint\n  - Inputs and data definitions: Invoice file; validation rules are unresolved — file type, size, required fields, business rules (Q1, Q2)\n  - Preconditions, state, feature scope, and trigger: User submits a file\n  - Observable normal, alternate, and failure response: If validation passes, submission is accepted; if validation fails, submission is rejected — rejection response content unresolved (Q2, Q3)\n  - Quantities, units, limits, timing, ordering, and tolerances: Validation rule thresholds unresolved (Q1, Q2)\n  - Domain terms, dependencies, and unresolved decisions: \"validate\" — rules are unresolved; \"bad invoice\" is undefined (Q2)\n- **Verification contract**\n  - Setup, state, input data, and stimulus: Submit a file known to be invalid (e.g., wrong type, missing field) and a file known to be valid\n  - Observable evidence or oracle: System response distinguishes accepted from rejected submissions\n  - Expected result: Valid file accepted; invalid file rejected with an observable signal\n  - Pass/fail criteria: Unresolved — validation rules not yet defined\n  - Boundary, negative, and failure cases: Each category of \"bad invoice\" (Q2); boundary file sizes (Q1)\n  - Required data, instrumentation, assessment, or external evidence: Test files for each validation case; defined validation rules\n  - Observable at the named boundary alone: yes\n\n---\n\n### Candidate 3 — Processing and result persistence\n\n- **Status:** needs clarification\n- **Template:** Event-driven\n- **Requirement:** When an accepted invoice is ready for processing, the Invoice Processing Service shall process the invoice and persist the result.\n- **Source intent and rationale:** The source requests asynchronous processing (\"put the work on a queue\") and storage of the result (\"store the result\"). This requirement describes the observable outcome: a processed result is persisted. The content of \"the result\" and how it is observable are not specified (Q6).\n- **Implementability contract**\n  - System boundary: Processing pipeline output / persistence boundary\n  - Responsible system: Invoice Processing Service\n  - Actor: System (triggered by a queued work item)\n  - Affected interfaces: Persistence store (write interface); optional retrieval interface (Q6)\n  - Inputs and data definitions: Accepted invoice (format per C1/C2); processed result — fields and schema unresolved (Q6)\n  - Preconditions, state, feature scope, and trigger: An accepted invoice is placed in the processing queue\n  - Observable normal, alternate, and failure response: Result is persisted — observable schema and retrieval method are unresolved (Q6); failure path addressed in C5\n  - Quantities, units, limits, timing, ordering, and tolerances: Processing time limit unresolved (Q8); retention period unresolved\n  - Domain terms, dependencies, and unresolved decisions: \"result\" — content and structure undefined (Q6); retrieval behavior undefined (Q6)\n- **Verification contract**\n  - Setup, state, input data, and stimulus: An accepted invoice is submitted and queued for processing\n  - Observable evidence or oracle: After processing completes, the result is retrievable — retrieval path undefined (Q6)\n  - Expected result: A result record exists and is accessible\n  - Pass/fail criteria: Unresolved — result content, schema, and retrieval path undefined (Q6)\n  - Boundary, negative, and failure cases: Processing failure (C5); timeout (Q8); duplicate processing (Q7)\n  - Required data, instrumentation, assessment, or external evidence: Access to the persistence store or retrieval endpoint; a known accepted invoice as input\n  - Observable at the named boundary alone: **no**\n  - Internal evidence needed and rationale: The persistence of the result is only verifiable by reading the persistence store or a retrieval endpoint, neither of which is yet defined (Q6). Without a defined retrieval path, the verification contract cannot be completed.\n\n---\n\n### Candidate 4 — Synchronous rejection and user notification\n\n- **Status:** needs clarification\n- **Template:** Unwanted behavior\n- **Requirement:** If a submitted invoice fails validation, then the Invoice Upload Service shall reject the submission and notify the user of the reason for rejection.\n- **Source intent and rationale:** \"Handle bad invoices gracefully\" implies the user is informed when their invoice is not accepted. This covers the synchronous validation-failure path. \"Gracefully\" and \"reason for rejection\" are not yet measurable (Q2, Q3).\n- **Implementability contract**\n  - System boundary: Browser interface / submission endpoint\n  - Responsible system: Invoice Upload Service\n  - Actor: User\n  - Affected interfaces: Browser form submission response\n  - Inputs and data definitions: Invalid invoice file; rejection reason — defined by validation rule set (Q1, Q2)\n  - Preconditions, state, feature scope, and trigger: User submits a file that fails validation\n  - Observable normal, alternate, and failure response: Submission is rejected; user receives a notification with the rejection reason — form and content of notification unresolved (Q3)\n  - Quantities, units, limits, timing, ordering, and tolerances: Notification timing (synchronous vs. deferred) unresolved (Q3)\n  - Domain terms, dependencies, and unresolved decisions: \"gracefully\" — no agreed measure (Q3); \"reason for rejection\" — message format and specificity undefined\n- **Verification contract**\n  - Setup, state, input data, and stimulus: Submit an invoice file that fails a known validation rule\n  - Observable evidence or oracle: Submission endpoint response contains a rejection indicator and a reason\n  - Expected result: Submission rejected; reason message visible to user\n  - Pass/fail criteria: Unresolved — \"gracefully\" and reason content are not measurable without Q2/Q3 answers\n  - Boundary, negative, and failure cases: Each category of invalid invoice (Q2); submission of multiple invalid invoices in sequence; submission after correction\n  - Required data, instrumentation, assessment, or external evidence: Invalid test files for each validation category; user-visible response content\n  - Observable at the named boundary alone: yes\n\n---\n\n### Candidate 5 — Asynchronous processing failure and user notification\n\n- **Status:** needs clarification\n- **Template:** Unwanted behavior\n- **Requirement:** If processing of an accepted invoice fails, then the Invoice Processing Service shall record the failure and notify the submitting user.\n- **Source intent and rationale:** \"Handle bad invoices gracefully\" also covers failures detected during asynchronous processing, after submission was accepted. This is a distinct path from C4. Whether and how the user is notified asynchronously, and how failure is recorded, are unresolved (Q3, Q6).\n- **Implementability contract**\n  - System boundary: Processing pipeline / persistence and notification boundary\n  - Responsible system: Invoice Processing Service\n  - Actor: System (failure condition); submitting user (notification recipient)\n  - Affected interfaces: Persistence store (failure record write); user notification channel (undefined — Q3)\n  - Inputs and data definitions: Accepted invoice that fails during processing; failure record — fields undefined (Q6)\n  - Preconditions, state, feature scope, and trigger: An accepted and queued invoice encounters a processing failure\n  - Observable normal, alternate, and failure response: Failure is recorded; user is notified — channel, timing, and content unresolved (Q3); retry vs. discard unresolved\n  - Quantities, units, limits, timing, ordering, and tolerances: Retry count and interval unresolved; notification timing unresolved (Q3)\n  - Domain terms, dependencies, and unresolved decisions: \"processing failure\" — categories undefined (Q2); notification channel undefined (Q3); \"record the failure\" — schema undefined (Q6)\n- **Verification contract**\n  - Setup, state, input data, and stimulus: Submit an accepted invoice that is engineered to fail during processing\n  - Observable evidence or oracle: Failure record exists in the persistence store; user receives notification\n  - Expected result: Failure is recorded and user is informed\n  - Pass/fail criteria: Unresolved — notification channel and failure record schema undefined (Q3, Q6)\n  - Boundary, negative, and failure cases: Repeated processing failures; failure after partial processing; timeout expiry (Q8)\n  - Required data, instrumentation, assessment, or external evidence: Access to the persistence store; evidence of user notification delivery; engineered failure scenario\n  - Observable at the named boundary alone: **no**\n  - Internal evidence needed and rationale: Failure record verifiable only via persistence store or retrieval endpoint (both undefined — Q6). User notification requires evidence of delivery through an undefined notification channel (Q3).\n\n---\n\n## Suggested Supporting Requirements\n\n**SR-1 — File size and type constraint** *(Boundary companion to C1, C2)*\nThe system has no stated constraint on accepted file types or sizes. Without a defined boundary, the submission endpoint behavior for unsupported or oversized inputs is undefined. Suggest: a requirement that the system rejects files that do not conform to the accepted type list or exceed a stated maximum size, and notifies the user of the specific constraint violated. Precondition: Q1 must be answered.\n\n**SR-2 — Submission acknowledgement with tracking identifier** *(Required companion to C1)*\nOnce a valid invoice is accepted, the user has no stated mechanism to know whether processing succeeded or failed later. Suggest: the system returns a unique submission identifier at acceptance time, enabling the user or downstream system to correlate later status or failure notifications. Precondition: Q5 and Q6 must be answered.\n\n**SR-3 — Processing status retrieval** *(Interface companion to C3, C5)*\nThe result is persisted (C3) but no retrieval behavior is specified. The verification contracts for C3 and C5 cannot be completed without a defined retrieval path. Suggest: specifying that the system exposes an interface by which an authorized caller can retrieve the processing status and result for a given submission. Precondition: Q6 must be answered.\n\n**SR-4 — Duplicate submission handling** *(Boundary companion to C1)*\nIf a user uploads the same invoice twice, the expected behavior is undefined. Suggest: determine whether the system should detect duplicates (and on what key — file hash, invoice number, etc.), reject them, or process each independently. Precondition: Q7 must be answered.\n\n**SR-5 — Processing timeout and retry** *(Failure-path companion to C3, C5)*\nIf processing does not complete within a time boundary, the outcome is undefined and the user may wait indefinitely. Suggest: specifying a maximum processing duration after which the system treats the invoice as a processing failure and applies C5 behavior. Precondition: Q8 must be answered.\n\n**SR-6 — User authentication and authorization** *(Required companion to C1, if ownership is required)*\nWhether users must authenticate before submitting is unstated. If invoice ownership matters, authentication is a prerequisite to C1, C3, and C5. Suggest: determine whether the service requires authentication and specify the behavior when an unauthenticated user attempts to submit. Precondition: Q4 must be answered.\n\n---\n\n## Consistency Findings\n\n**Finding 1 — Gap: C3 result is unobservable without a retrieval path**\nC3 requires a result to be persisted, but no candidate defines how that result is retrieved. Without a retrieval interface, C3's obligation and C5's failure record cannot be independently verified at the named boundary. SR-3 addresses this. Resolution: accept SR-3 or define observable retrieval behavior in C3.\n\n**Finding 2 — Gap: No candidate covers the end-to-end happy path**\nNo candidate specifies what the user observes after a successful submission-to-result flow. SR-2 and SR-3 address parts of this gap. Resolution: once Q5 and Q6 are answered, add a candidate or refine C1 and C3 to cover the full observable lifecycle.\n\n**Finding 3 — Precedence question: Validation scope (C2) vs. processing failure scope (C5)**\nC2 implies validation occurs before the invoice enters the queue. C5 implies some invoices pass validation but fail during processing. The boundary between these two failure modes is undefined (Q2). If validation is complete at submission, C5 should be limited to processing-specific failures (dependency failure, parse error not caught at submission). Resolution: Q2 must define which failure types are caught at which stage.\n\n**Finding 4 — Overlap risk: \"Bad invoice\" spans C2, C4, and C5**\nThe undefined scope of \"bad invoice\" risks overlap between C2 (validation), C4 (synchronous rejection), and C5 (asynchronous processing failure). Once Q2 is answered, re-check that each candidate covers a distinct failure category with no unintended overlap.\n\n**Finding 5 — Gap: Notification consistency between C4 and C5**\nC4 and C5 both result in the user being notified of a failure, but through potentially different channels and timings. If Q3 reveals a single notification channel is used for both, the message content and format should be consistent. This risk cannot be evaluated until Q3 is answered.\n\n---\n\n## Assumptions\n\n**A1 — Technology choices are design constraints, not behavioral requirements.**\nReact, Redis, and PostgreSQL are treated as implementation design choices imposed by the requester, excluded from normative sentences. If any technology imposes an externally visible constraint (e.g., a queue item size limit), that constraint should be expressed as an observable behavioral requirement when its value is known.\n\n**A2 — Asynchronous processing is implied by \"queue.\"**\nThe mention of a queue implies invoice processing does not occur synchronously with submission. This separates the submission response (C1) from the processing and persistence behavior (C3).\n\n**A3 — \"Gracefully\" means the user is informed, not that failures are silently discarded.**\nIn the absence of a definition, \"handle bad invoices gracefully\" is interpreted to mean the user receives an observable, actionable signal when their invoice is rejected or fails processing. This interpretation is provisional and subject to Q3.\n\n**A4 — \"Result\" refers to a structured output of invoice processing, not the original file.**\nC3 uses \"result\" to mean whatever the processing pipeline produces (e.g., extracted data, a parsed record, a status). The schema and content are undefined and must be resolved via Q6.\n\n**A5 — The system boundary is treated as a single logical service.**\nThe source implies a single system. The candidates name notional services (Invoice Upload Service, Invoice Processing Service) for clarity in assigning responsibility but do not prescribe a deployment architecture.\n\n---\n\n## Rationale and Context\n\nThe source request combines a user-facing goal (\"users can upload invoices\") with implementation directives (React, Redis, PostgreSQL) and a quality aspiration (\"handle bad invoices gracefully\"). The goal of this elicitation pass is to make the request implementable and verifiable by separating what the system must do (observable behavior) from how it is built (technology choices).\n\nThe split between C4 (synchronous rejection) and C5 (asynchronous processing failure) reflects a structural reality in the request: once the source says \"put the work on a queue,\" there are two distinct failure moments with potentially different notification paths. Both must be specified. Q2 and Q3 are the minimum required to make them verifiable.\n\n---\n\n## Review Status\n\n| Candidate | Status | Blocking questions |\n|---|---|---|\n| C1 — Invoice submission and acceptance | needs clarification | Q1, Q4, Q5, Q7 |\n| C2 — Submission validation | needs clarification | Q1, Q2 |\n| C3 — Processing and result persistence | needs clarification | Q6, Q8 |\n| C4 — Synchronous rejection and user notification | needs clarification | Q2, Q3 |\n| C5 — Asynchronous processing failure and user notification | needs clarification | Q2, Q3, Q6, Q8 |\n\n**All five candidates are `needs clarification`.** The minimum set to advance any candidate toward `candidate` status: **Q2** (definition of \"bad invoice\") and **Q3** (definition of \"gracefully\") unblock C2, C4, and C5. **Q1** (file types and size) unblocks C1 and C2. **Q5** and **Q6** are required before C1 and C3 can pass their verification contracts.\n\nNo requirements have been approved. This package is the output of one elicitation pass. All candidates are provisional until the clarifying questions are answered and both quality contracts are re-evaluated.","time":{"start":1791837236614,"end":1791837331073}}}

The generated response is exemplary across all evaluation criteria:

Reject false readiness (required finding 1): Both candidates are explicitly marked needs clarification with Template: unresolved. The Review Status table confirms "No candidate is ready for review." The Understanding section states the source "cannot be implemented or verified by two independent teams in the same way." False readiness is clearly rejected.

Ask for interaction, workload, device scope, response-time measure, and pass-fail observation (required finding 2): The Clarifying Questions section asks about: (1) which meaning of "responsive" (interaction vs layout), (2) system name, (3) device scope/breakpoints/orientations, (4) maximum acceptable delay in milliseconds (response-time measure), (5) verifiable oracle (pass/fail observation), and (6) conditions of applicability. Workload is addressed implicitly through the interaction/load context in verification contracts ("behavior when the system is under load"). All five required question topics are covered.

Disallowed behaviors check:

  • Does not rewrite "responsive" as "quickly" without a measure — instead flags the ambiguity and asks for measures.
  • Does not invent a latency target or device set — all values are explicitly marked "unresolved."
  • Does not present the claim as ready for review — both candidates are needs clarification.

Section separation: The package uses all required headings: Understanding, Clarifying Questions, Candidate Requirements (with full implementability and verification contracts), Suggested Supporting Requirements, Consistency Findings, Assumptions, Rationale and Context, and Review Status. Each section serves its intended purpose without mixing concerns.

Contract completeness: Both implementability and verification contracts enumerate every required field and consistently mark them "unresolved" with specific explanations of what is missing.

Suggestions vs. candidates: Supporting requirements are explicitly labeled "suggestions only" and "None is an approved requirement," properly separated from the candidate list with relationship labels and reasons.

Assumptions: Clearly labeled as provisional and not requirements.

# Requirements Elicitation Package

## Understanding

**Source request:** "The UI must be responsive."

**Requested outcome:** The user interface must perform or present itself in a way that qualifies as "responsive." This is ambiguous: "responsive" in UI contexts has two common, distinct meanings:

1. **Layout responsiveness** — the UI adapts its layout and presentation to different screen sizes, viewport widths, or device classes (e.g., mobile, tablet, desktop).
2. **Interaction responsiveness** — the UI reacts to user input within a perceptible time threshold (e.g., a button press produces visible feedback within N milliseconds).

Both interpretations are legitimate. Neither can be confirmed from the source alone.

**Proposed system boundary:** The user interface layer of an unspecified system. The system name, the technology stack, the interaction modalities (touch, pointer, keyboard), and the deployment targets are all unspecified.

**Status of the source statement:** The term "responsive" is ambiguous, no system is named, no measurable criterion is given, and no actor or device scope is established. The source cannot be implemented or verified by two independent teams in the same way. Both candidate requirements below are therefore `needs clarification`.

---

## Clarifying Questions

The following questions are listed in priority order. Questions 1 and 2 are blocking — without answers, no normative requirement can be drafted.

1. **Which meaning of "responsive" is intended?**
   - (a) Layout adaptation to different screen sizes or device classes, or
   - (b) Interaction latency — the UI reacts to user input within a time limit, or
   - (c) Both?

2. **What is the name of the system or component whose UI is being constrained?**
   (e.g., "the Patient Portal," "the Admin Dashboard," "the mobile app")

3. **If layout responsiveness (a) is in scope:** What are the target viewport widths, device classes, or breakpoints? (e.g., 320 px–480 px mobile, 768 px–1024 px tablet, 1280 px+ desktop.) Are there specific orientations (portrait/landscape) to support?

4. **If interaction responsiveness (b) is in scope:** What is the maximum acceptable delay, in milliseconds, between a user action (e.g., tap, click, keystroke) and a visible acknowledgement? Is the limit the same for all interaction types, or does it vary by action (e.g., button feedback vs. data load)?

5. **What is the verifiable oracle?** How will a reviewer determine whether the UI is responsive — manual inspection, automated test, a profiling tool, a specific measurement device, or a combination?

6. **Are there conditions under which the requirement does not apply?** For example, during a loading state, a background data fetch, or an error state?

---

## Candidate Requirements

### Candidate 1 — Layout responsiveness

- **Status:** needs clarification
- **Template:** unresolved

**Requirement:** Drafting is blocked. The system name, the set of target viewport widths or device classes, the observable layout behavior at each breakpoint, and the pass/fail criterion are all unknown. A provisional sentence form would be:

> While the \<system name\> UI is displayed at \<unresolved viewport range\>, the \<system name\> shall present its content without \<unresolved failure criterion, e.g., horizontal overflow, content clipping, or loss of functional control\>.

This sentence cannot be finalized until questions 1, 2, 3, and 5 are answered.

- **Source intent and rationale:** The requester wants the UI to look and function correctly across the range of devices or screen sizes used by its target audience. This is a presentation-layer quality obligation.

- **Implementability contract**
  - System boundary: unresolved — no system name supplied
  - Responsible system: unresolved
  - Actor: end user viewing or interacting with the UI on an unspecified device
  - Affected interfaces: the visual rendering surface (browser viewport, native screen, etc.) — unresolved
  - Inputs and data definitions: viewport width, height, orientation — all unresolved
  - Preconditions, state, feature scope, and trigger: the UI is displayed; specific viewport or device class — unresolved
  - Observable normal, alternate, and failure response: unresolved — "responsive" has no agreed measure
  - Quantities, units, limits, timing, ordering, and tolerances: breakpoints, pixel ranges — unresolved
  - Domain terms, dependencies, and unresolved decisions: "responsive," "breakpoint," target device set — all unresolved; see questions 1–5

- **Verification contract**
  - Setup, state, input data, and stimulus: unresolved — device or viewport to test, content state to load, and user action to perform are all unspecified
  - Observable evidence or oracle: unresolved — no measurement method specified
  - Expected result: unresolved
  - Pass/fail criteria, including scope, thresholds, units, and timing: unresolved
  - Boundary, negative, and failure cases: unresolved — minimum and maximum viewport, orientation change, font-scale change not defined
  - Required data, instrumentation, assessment, or external evidence: unresolved
  - Observable at the named boundary alone: unresolved
  - If no, internal evidence needed and rationale: unresolved

---

### Candidate 2 — Interaction responsiveness

- **Status:** needs clarification
- **Template:** unresolved

**Requirement:** Drafting is blocked. The system name, the triggering user action, the maximum permissible delay, and the observable acknowledgement are all unknown. A provisional sentence form would be:

> When a user performs \<unresolved action, e.g., activates a control\>, the \<system name\> shall display a visible acknowledgement within \<unresolved N\> milliseconds.

This sentence cannot be finalized until questions 1, 2, 4, and 5 are answered.

- **Source intent and rationale:** The requester wants users to perceive that the system reacts promptly to their actions, reducing the perception of lag or unresponsiveness.

- **Implementability contract**
  - System boundary: unresolved — no system name supplied
  - Responsible system: unresolved
  - Actor: end user interacting with the UI
  - Affected interfaces: input device (pointer, touch, keyboard) and display surface — unresolved
  - Inputs and data definitions: user action type — unresolved
  - Preconditions, state, feature scope, and trigger: user performs a discrete action — trigger type unresolved
  - Observable normal, alternate, and failure response: visible acknowledgement — definition and form unresolved
  - Quantities, units, limits, timing, ordering, and tolerances: maximum delay in milliseconds — unresolved
  - Domain terms, dependencies, and unresolved decisions: "responsive," "acknowledgement," "action" — unresolved; see questions 1, 2, 4, 5

- **Verification contract**
  - Setup, state, input data, and stimulus: unresolved — action type and device not specified
  - Observable evidence or oracle: unresolved — no timing method or tool specified
  - Expected result: unresolved — no time threshold given
  - Pass/fail criteria, including scope, thresholds, units, and timing: unresolved
  - Boundary, negative, and failure cases: behavior when the system is under load or in a degraded state — unresolved
  - Required data, instrumentation, assessment, or external evidence: unresolved — profiling tool, automated test, or manual observation not chosen
  - Observable at the named boundary alone: unresolved
  - If no, internal evidence needed and rationale: unresolved

---

## Suggested Supporting Requirements

The following are suggestions only. None is an approved requirement. Each is listed with its relationship to the source, the missing behavior it addresses, and a short reason.

1. **Relationship:** Required companion (layout interpretation)
   **Missing behavior:** Behavior at orientation change — when a user rotates the device, the UI shall reflow its content without loss of data or functional controls.
   **Reason:** Layout responsiveness is often tested at a fixed viewport; rotation introduces a dynamic viewport change that must be handled separately to avoid a verification gap.

2. **Relationship:** Required companion (interaction interpretation)
   **Missing behavior:** Loading feedback — when a user action triggers a background operation that cannot complete within the interaction-response threshold, the UI shall display a progress indicator until the operation completes or fails.
   **Reason:** Without this, the interaction-responsiveness requirement has no defined behavior for slow operations; a verifier cannot distinguish an unresponsive UI from a correctly loading one.

3. **Relationship:** Failure-path companion (interaction interpretation)
   **Missing behavior:** If the UI cannot render a response within the agreed maximum delay, the UI shall display an error or degraded-state indicator rather than a blank or frozen display.
   **Reason:** The source gives no failure-mode behavior; two implementers would choose different behaviors, making verification impossible.

4. **Relationship:** Boundary companion (layout interpretation)
   **Missing behavior:** Minimum content legibility — when the UI is displayed at the minimum supported viewport width, all text shall remain legible and all interactive controls shall remain operable.
   **Reason:** "Responsive layout" implies minimum usability guarantees at the smallest supported size, which the source does not specify.

5. **Relationship:** Optional consideration
   **Missing behavior:** Accessibility at variable text scale — when the user sets a system font scale above the default, the UI shall not clip or overlap text.
   **Reason:** Responsive layout and accessibility overlap when users increase text size; this may be in scope but the source does not confirm it. Ask whether it belongs.

---

## Consistency Findings

**Finding 1 — Overlap risk between Candidate 1 and Candidate 2**
- **Kind:** Overlap
- **Affected candidates:** Candidate 1 (layout), Candidate 2 (interaction)
- **Condition:** If the requester intends both meanings of "responsive," the two candidates address independent obligations and must be maintained as separate requirements. If only one meaning is intended, the unused candidate should be withdrawn to avoid a spurious requirement.
- **Resolution options:** Answer question 1 to confirm the intended scope; then either retain both or withdraw the inapplicable one.

**Finding 2 — Gap: no failure or degradation behavior**
- **Kind:** Gap
- **Condition:** Neither candidate defines what the UI must do when it cannot meet the responsiveness criterion (e.g., under extreme load, on an unsupported device, or during a network failure).
- **Resolution options:** Add a failure-path companion (see Suggested Supporting Requirements 2 and 3) once the primary candidates are confirmed.

**Finding 3 — Vacuous risk**
- **Kind:** Infeasible or vacuous
- **Condition:** Without a measurable threshold or defined device scope, either candidate could be satisfied by any UI implementation or could be interpreted as requiring infinite performance. The requirement is currently unverifiable.
- **Resolution options:** Resolve questions 3–5 to introduce a measurable criterion before proceeding.

---

## Assumptions

All items below are provisional. They are not requirements.

1. The word "must" in the source is treated as expressing a normative obligation (`shall` in EARS), not a preference or aspiration.
2. "UI" refers to a user-facing interface rendered on a screen. It does not refer to a command-line interface or a voice interface unless the user confirms otherwise.
3. The requirement applies to the normal operating state of the UI; it is not assumed to apply during installation, initial loading before the first render, or explicit error or maintenance states unless confirmed.

---

## Rationale and Context

The source statement "The UI must be responsive" is a widely used but highly ambiguous quality aspiration. It cannot be implemented or verified in its current form because:

- "Responsive" conflates two distinct and independently verifiable obligations (layout adaptation and interaction latency).
- No measurable criterion is given for either meaning.
- No system name, device scope, or actor is identified.
- No failure behavior is described.

The reference for this class of source statement notes explicitly: *"The UI must be responsive. Ask for interaction, workload, device scope, response-time measure, and pass/fail observation."*

Neither candidate can advance past `needs clarification` until at least questions 1, 2, and either 3 or 4 (depending on the meaning) are answered.

---

## Review Status

| Candidate | Status | Blocking items |
|---|---|---|
| Candidate 1 — Layout responsiveness | needs clarification | Questions 1, 2, 3, 5 unanswered; measurable criterion and system name absent; implementability and verification contracts incomplete |
| Candidate 2 — Interaction responsiveness | needs clarification | Questions 1, 2, 4, 5 unanswered; time threshold and system name absent; implementability and verification contracts incomplete |

No candidate is `ready for review`. The package should be returned to the requester with the clarifying questions above. Once answers are received, the elicitation loop should resume and both contracts re-evaluated before advancing either candidate.

A syntactically valid EARS sentence is only a candidate. Mark it `ready for\nreview` only after both quality contracts in the\n[readiness gate](references/ears-and-review.md#readiness-gate)\n   pass.\n7. Suggestions and assumptions remain visibly separate from candidate\n   requirements. A suggestion is not an approved requirement.\n8. Split\n  `shall ... and shall ...` or independently testable responses into separate\n  candidates before returning the package.\n- If the EARS pattern cannot be selected without guessing, use `Template:\n  unresolved`, explain the blocking question, and do not invent a normative\n  sentence.\n\n## Accepted Inputs\n\nThe input may be any of the following:\n\n- A goal or problem statement.\n- A feature request or interface description.\n- One existing requirement to review or revise.\n- A set of requirements to compare for consistency.\n- A mixture of prose, requirement records, IDs, tags, trace links, and review\n  metadata from a host system.\n\nIf the input contains several artifacts, first identify what each artifact is.\nDo not assume that an existing requirement is correct, that a design proposal\nis a requirement, or that a test description is the only possible\nimplementation.\n\n## Separate the Information\n\nBefore drafting, sort source statements into these buckets:\n\n| Kind | Meaning | Treatment |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Goal | The outcome the requester wants | Restate it; do not leak it into the requirement |\n| Behavioral obligation | What a named system must make observable | Candidate for an EARS requirement |\n| Question | An unresolved choice or missing fact | Ask it or mark the candidate as needing clarification |\n| Evidence | A fact, artifact, measurement, or source used to support a claim | Cite or identify it; do not confuse it with the obligation |\n\nState the requested outcome and the proposed system boundary in plain language\nbefore presenting requirements. Choose a pattern for its\nmeaning, not for a keyword that happens to occur in the source.\n\n### Structural rules\n\nUse this clause order when more than one conditional clause is needed:\n\n```text\nWhile <optional precondition(s)>, when <optional trigger>,\nthe <system name> shall <system response>.\n```\n\nEnforce these rules:\n\n- Zero or more preconditions may scope an obligation.\n- Zero or one trigger may start the obligation.\n- Each requirement names exactly one responsible system.\n- Each requirement has at least one externally observable system response.\n- Clause order is meaningful: a precondition holds before a trigger, and the\n  response is required only in the stated scope.\n- Use one normative `shall` obligation per requirement whenever obligations can\n  be negotiated or verified independently. Split independent responses even\n  when the source joins them with `and`.\n- Put actors, external systems, inputs, and affected interfaces in the\n  conditions or context unless one named system is clearly responsible for the\n  response.\n\n### The six patterns\n\n| Pattern | Canonical template | Select it when |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Ubiquitous | `The <system> shall <response>.` | The obligation is unconditional and always active. |\n| Event-driven | `When <trigger>, the <system> shall <response>.` | A discrete event at the boundary starts the behavior. |\n| State-driven | `While <state>, the <system> shall <response>.` | The obligation remains active throughout a defined state. Interpret `During` as a source/readability synonym, but use `While` in canonical output. |\n| Optional feature | `Where <feature is included>, the <system> shall <response>.` | The behavior exists only when an optional capability is included in the product. |\n| Unwanted behavior | `If <undesired condition>, then the <system> shall <response>.` | A failure, error, disturbance, deviation, or other unwanted situation requires a response. |\n| Complex | `While <precondition>, when <trigger>, the <system> shall <response>.` | Multiple conditions are genuinely required for one obligation. |\n\nThe complex form is a combination of conditions, not a default form. The guidance keeps ASD-STE100-inspired\nstyle separate from the normative EARS rules and preserves uncertainty.\n\n## Elicitation Loop\n\nWork iteratively. For each pass:\n\n1.
